likely: Candida species (colonization common, true infection less so)
possible: Polymicrobial flora, especially with long-term catheterization
pathogens.why: Catheter-associated UTI involves a broader and more resistant organism spectrum than uncomplicated cystitis due to biofilm formation on the catheter surface and selection pressure from prior antibiotic exposure, with polymicrobial infection common in long-term catheterization.

investigations.test: Urine culture (from newly placed catheter if replacing, or freshly collected sample)
investigations.why: Essential given the high resistance burden and biofilm-related polymicrobial colonization in this population — guides definitive therapy.
CA-UTI can be a source of bacteremia/urosepsis; positive cultures confirm systemic involvement.
Baseline assessment, particularly relevant if upper tract involvement (pyelonephritis) is suspected.
